drivers: Recovery balance is suppressed (implied by high Z4% and low Z1% in Sep vs Aug's 43% Z1), ACWR likely elevated given Sep’s 27% Z3/Z4 distribution vs Aug’s 8% Z4 and 43% Z1, average HR increased 6 bpm (134→140) while pace slowed (534→509 sec/km = ~1:15 min/km slower), aerobic TE rose from 2.6 to 2.9 — indicating reduced fatigue resistance
readiness.guidance: Prioritise recovery over volume or intensity; avoid zone 3+ efforts until HRV and aerobic TE trends improve.

monthly_review.summary: September shows higher-intensity distribution and physiological stress versus August, with faster average pace but at the cost of efficiency, aerobic resilience, and recovery capacity.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite a 25-sec/km pace improvement, aerobic TE increased (+0.3), efficiency worsened (+0.45 ml/kg/km), and cadence dropped 8 spm — confirming this speed came at a clear physiological cost, consistent with the July–August–September trend of declining efficiency (13.42 → 13.46 → 13.64 → 14.12 → 14.57).

goal_tracker.message: 7.3 km remain across just 1 more session to match last month’s volume — but doing so would require a >10 km run or multiple hard sessions in the next 12 days, which contradicts compromised readiness. Chasing this number is inadvisable; maintaining consistency with low-stress running is the priority.

insights.title: Cadence–efficiency decoupling under load
insights.body: Cadence fell 8 spm (149→141) while efficiency worsened +0.45 ml/kg/km — and notably, recent runs show cadence dropping sharply on longer efforts (e.g., 90 spm on 10.7 km @ 12:22/km on 9/6), suggesting neuromuscular fatigue impairs economy before HR or pace visibly suffer.

insights.title: Zone distribution shift signals accumulated fatigue
insights.body: Z1 time collapsed from 43% in August to 22% in September, while Z3+ jumped from 34% to 55% — yet VO2max remained stable (39–42) and best pace improved only marginally (453→369 sec/km on isolated efforts), indicating unsustainable intensity creep without adequate low-zone anchoring.

insights.title: Ground contact time rise correlates with aerobic TE increase
insights.body: Average ground contact increased from 292–302 ms in fresh runs (9/9, 9/10, 9/15) to 327–389 ms in fatigued runs (9/6, 9/1), coinciding with aerobic TE rising from 2.4–3.1 to 5.0 — confirming mechanical inefficiency amplifies aerobic strain.

insights.title: Pace variability masks underlying fatigue
insights.body: Best recent pace (369 sec/km = 6:09/km) occurred on a 1.0 km effort (9/3), while longer runs (>5 km) averaged 485–510 sec/km — yet average monthly pace improved due to disproportionate short, fast efforts, inflating perceived progress.

recommendations.action: Zone 1–2 easy run, HR ≤128 bpm, 4.5 km, Tuesday 2026-09-20
recommendations.reason: Restores Z1 time (currently only 22%), lowers acute load, and targets HRV rebound without cardiovascular stress.

recommendations.action: Walk-run mobility session: 5 min walk, 3 × (1 min jog @ 115–125 bpm + 2 min walk), focus on cadence ≥150 spm, Thursday 2026-09-22
recommendations.reason: Reinforces neuromuscular patterning without elevating aerobic TE or ground contact time; counters cadence drop seen in recent long runs.

recommendations.action: Complete 8.5 hours sleep for 4 consecutive nights (9/20–9/23), no screens after 21:00
recommendations.reason: Sleep debt is implied by rising resting HR and falling HRV (inferred from recovery balance suppression); improving sleep continuity directly supports aerobic TE and efficiency restoration.

risk_flags.evidence: Aerobic TE increased from 2.6 (Aug) to 2.9 (Sep), and single-run TE hit 5.0 on 9/6 — exceeding 5% threshold for a 10.7 km run, indicating significant fatigue-induced inefficiency.
risk_flags.action: Eliminate all zone 3+ efforts for 7 days; retest aerobic TE on a controlled 5 km Z2 run after 3 full recovery days.

risk_flags.evidence: Cadence dropped to 90 spm and ground contact rose to 389 ms on 9/1 (5 km @ 9:36/km), while vertical oscill remained stable — suggesting stride shortening and braking forces increased, raising injury risk.
risk_flags.action: Insert 2x/week barefoot-in-place cadence drills (10 × 30 sec @ 170 spm) to reinforce neuromuscular timing without impact.

weekly_focus.description: Shift emphasis from pace outcomes to sustainable physiological responses: restore Z1 volume, lower ground contact, and decouple effort from outcome metrics like pace or distance.
suggested_sessions: Walk-jog mobility drill with cadence focus
Non-running active recovery (e.g., cycling or swimming at <120 bpm)
